title: Which multiples of forty lie in this stretch?
description: Skip counting in forty gives the multiples of forty, and only the jumps that land between three hundred ten and four hundred ten are kept. A check shows each kept number is forty more than the one before.
teaching_notes: One idea: list the multiples of forty near the stretch and keep those inside it. Watch for students who forget that four hundred also lies in the stretch.

source: Figure it Out box 2, Q1, p.111
video_script.why: The child counts on in forty and keeps only the multiples that lie between the two end numbers.
video_script.substitution: Find the multiples of a number in a stretch by counting on in that number and keeping those inside the stretch.
video_script.anchor: a number strip with jumps of forty between three hundred and ten and four hundred and ten
video_script.payoff_line: The multiples are three hundred and twenty, three hundred and sixty and four hundred

final_answer.spoken: the multiples are three hundred and twenty, three hundred and sixty and four hundred

maths_rules: 280 is below 310 and 440 is above 410, so both are left out
video_script.design: One idea: skip counting in forty and keeping the landings inside the stretch. Same method as the book example: multiples come by skip counting.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a number strip with the numbers 310 and 410 marked

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.ask: the strip appears with 310 and 410 marked and a question mark between them

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about multiples of forty.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which multiples of forty lie between three hundred and ten and four hundred and ten?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: jumps of 40 along a number strip, each landing glowing

marks.way: the example from the book is pointed to
marks.jump: jumps of 40 are drawn along the strip
marks.range: the stretch between 310 and 410 is shaded

narration: <bookmark mark='way'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='jump'/>Multiples of forty come by skip counting in jumps of forty.
<bookmark mark='range'/>We look for the jumps that land between the two end numbers.

beats.on_screen: Given: multiples of 40; the numbers between 310 and 410

marks.given: the two end numbers are written under the word Given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, jumps of forty, and the numbers between three hundred and ten and four hundred and ten.

beats.on_screen: To find: all the multiples of 40 between 310 and 410

marks.find: the words To find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find all the multiples of forty in that stretch.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 40 x 7 = 280, below 310, so it is left out
narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step one, start with forty times seven, which is two hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='out'/>That is below three hundred and ten, so it is left out.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 40 x 8 = 320, 40 x 9 = 360, 40 x 10 = 400; all three lie between 310 and 410

marks.count: 40 x 8 = 320 is written and the landing glows
marks.more: 40 x 9 = 360 and 40 x 10 = 400 are written and the landings glow

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step two, count on in forty. Forty times eight is three hundred and twenty.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Forty times nine is three hundred and sixty, and forty times ten is four hundred.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 40 x 11 = 440, above 410, so we stop
narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step three, try the next jump. Forty times eleven is four hundred and forty.
<bookmark mark='stop'/>It is above four hundred and ten, so we stop here.

marks.in: the three numbers are shown inside the shaded stretch

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Step four, check the three numbers. Each is forty more than the one before.
<bookmark mark='in'/>All three lie between three hundred and ten and four hundred and ten.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the multiples of 40 are 320, 360 and 400
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The multiples are three hundred and twenty, three hundred and sixty and four hundred.
